text_blocks.snippet: Kidney disease awareness is crucial because millions are affected by this condition, often unknowingly. March is National Kidney Month, a time dedicated to raising awareness about kidney health and the vital role kidneys play in overall well-being. Understanding the risk factors, symptoms, and prevention strategies is key to early detection and slowing the progression of kidney disease.
snippet_highlighted_words: March is National Kidney Month, a time dedicated to raising awareness about kidney health and the vital role kidneys play in overall well-being

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of kidney disease awareness:

list.title: Understanding Kidney Function:
list.snippet: Kidneys filter waste, excess fluids, and toxins from the blood, maintaining the body's overall balance.

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Age, family history, health conditions like diabetes and high blood pressure, certain ethnicities, and lifestyle choices (like overuse of certain medications) can increase risk.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms can include dry, itchy skin, muscle cramps, swelling in the feet and ankles, decreased urination, trouble breathing or sleeping, nausea, and loss of appetite.

list.title: Early Detection:
list.snippet: Regular checkups and blood tests (like the eGFR test) can help detect kidney disease early.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Maintaining a healthy weight, managing blood pressure and blood sugar, staying hydrated, and avoiding smoking and excessive alcohol consumption can help protect kidney health, according to Century Medical & Dental Center.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Early diagnosis allows for interventions to slow the progression of kidney disease and potentially delay the need for dialysis or transplant.

list.title: Support:
list.snippet: Organizations like the National Kidney Foundation offer resources, support, and advocacy for those affected by kidney disease.
